Turns the feature-service composition standard from a document nothing enforced into one that fails the build. WHAT THE OLD GUARD DID: src/test/feature-service-composition-standard.test.ts asserted that the standard's DOCUMENTATION still contained certain sentences and that three modules still exported certain names. It inspected no service, hook or page, so it would have passed unchanged with every service in the repository violating every rule in the standard. Two assertions were worse than weak - they pinned createIdempotentRequest as a required export and as required documentation while that helper had ZERO production call sites, so the test was actively protecting dead code. That test file is now reduced to a document-existence guard, which is the one thing a source scan genuinely cannot do. THE SPLIT, BY CAPABILITY RATHER THAN BY TOOL. A source scan is a poor guard for a single-token rule - hand-built messages, runs after a full build, re-implements directory walking - and a good one for a rule needing cross-file knowledge or an ABSENCE check, which no-restricted-syntax cannot express. PHASE 1, ESLint, LANDS GREEN: a block scoped to the contract-only service set (13 module *.service.ts plus the 3 shared transports = 16 files) adding no-restricted-imports for TanStack Query/Zustand/React/the toast manager and no-restricted-syntax for axios.create, raw fetch, .interceptors, new QueryClient, cache writes and invalidation, normalizeApiError/isConflictError, useNavigate/usePermission and a literal 'Idempotency-Key'. Measured 0 violations across all 16 files before landing, so it is a pure regression fence - and a fence rather than a formality, since these are the imports a service acquires casually while 'just fixing' a feature. The globs are load-bearingly narrow: src/modules/**/services/** also matches auth/session-lifecycle.ts and auth/active-scope-context.ts, which legitimately own the QueryClient and the auth session key the standard assigns to the auth module, giving two false positives on day one. PHASE 2, the real violations: count.service.ts was the ONLY service interpolating a path parameter without encodeURIComponent and had six bare path constants with no satisfies keyof paths, so TypeScript never checked one; adjustment.service.ts had five more for the same reason; use-external-party-mutations.ts defined a local createIdempotencyKey shadowing the shared export AND hand-built the header at the call site, which the standard forbids BY NAME - the service now takes a plain key and attaches it with withIdempotencyKey. pathWithId itself existed as EIGHT identical three-line copies and count.service.ts was about to be the ninth; it is now src/shared/services/api-path.ts. PHASE 3, three scans in one file on hoisted helpers (src/test/support/source-scan.ts, lifted out of immutable-ledgers-audit.test.tsx so the repo has one way to scan source rather than a third style): query keys must come from a factory (checks the MISTAKE not the correct shape, so it cannot go stale when scopeParts changes); a failed secondary read must stay distinguishable (a bare ?? null scan is useless at 172 hits, so it correlates the collapse with the ABSENCE of an error branch for the SAME query variable, because file-scoped correlation false-positives on any two-component file); and an idempotency key is minted once per user intent - deliberately NOT 'inside mutationFn', which flags the three BEST implementations in the repo that mint inside the mutation and hold the result in a useRef. All three landed only after the violations they report were fixed: four hand-derived query keys and five unsafe key mints. Landing a red scan to raise awareness is how a guard dies. NON-VACUITY, THE WHOLE POINT, each verified by deliberately breaking what it guards. An exact file-count assertion per scan rather than > 0, because a narrowed glob leaves a handful of files not none. A negative control per scan running a known-bad snippet through the detector at the moment the suite executes - which caught a real flaw: the scan-3 control had its own simplified copy of the logic and had DRIFTED from the implementation, reporting one match per window line while the real rule reported one per violation; both now go through one function, because a control exercising different code than production proves nothing about the detector. Repo-relative offender lists so a failure names the file. And the standard-allow escape hatch, which had ZERO users and therefore trivially green tests: planting a violation with a marker above it kept the scan green, removing the marker turned it red naming file:line - which also found a genuine gap, since a marker excused only its own line while these constructs are multi-line, so the escape hatch looked like it worked and did not; it now excuses a four-line window. A marker without a real reason is rejected and the set is asserted to stay at 3 or fewer, because a rule needing more exceptions is the wrong rule. The ESLint block was verified the same way: a probe adding fetch() and new QueryClient() to a service produced 2 errors at exact lines, and green returned when removed. PHASE 4: createIdempotentRequest is DELETED. It bundled key creation and header attachment into one object, which cannot work here - a hook cannot hand an Axios config to a service, because the service is the only holder of the client. So the split is by design (the hook mints and holds a key, the service attaches the header) and the standard's retry rule was AMENDED to describe it, with the t09 verification doc's quote updated. The IdempotentRequest TYPE stays, still widely used by the document transport.
